clue.text: Assumes a leading role

parts.note: taking on the part of someone who leads others along a route or through a process

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes the lead and shows others the way is performing as a pathfinder for them.

clue.text: It's a hold-up, bud!

parts.note: reads like a robber's warning to a pal, but describes the ring of sepals that cups and supports a flower bud

explanation.definitionFit: The whorl of sepals at a flower's base encloses and supports the developing bud.

clue.text: Defer putting us back on dole

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another is placed above it
back says the little word us is turned round to read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
to dole out money is to pay it out, to spend

explanation.surface: Someone tries to postpone being put back on unemployment benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns US into SU, and 'on' sets it above SPEND in this down entry. In Britain 'the dole' is unemployment benefit, which is the surface sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off or hold over a decision is to postpone it.

clue.text: Display energy in extra-strong porter

indicators.note: in says the energy symbol is placed within the beer word

parts.note: stout was originally the name for an extra-strong porter beer
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A display of vigour after drinking a very strong dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things for show is to lay them out on view.

clue.text: In no way like a sovereign

definitions.text: In no way like a sovereign

parts.words: In no way like a sovereign
parts.note: describes behaviour utterly unbefitting a monarch

explanation.definitionFit: Conduct unworthy of a monarch is the opposite of regal.

clue.text: Giving a hand to a number of genial disposition

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Lending a helping hand to someone of a kindly temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals rearranging GENIAL into EALING, which follows D.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the dealer is the one handing out each player's cards.

clue.text: Award to raise the spirit but not inebriate

definitions.text: Award to raise the spirit but not inebriate

parts.words: Award to raise the spirit but not inebriate
parts.note: a trophy that uplifts, recalling the old phrase for tea as the drink that cheers but does not intoxicate

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from the poet Cowper, describing tea as the drink 'that cheers but not inebriates'.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional jocular name for tea, the beverage that lifts mood without making anyone drunk.

clue.text: Transport subject to inflation

parts.note: suggests fares rising with prices, but describes craft that fly once filled with hot air or gas

explanation.definitionFit: Hot-air craft carry passengers aloft only after their envelopes are blown up.

clue.text: Intend covering the whole course

parts.note: to mean to do something is to set out to do it; the whole course runs from beginning to end

explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning from the very beginning right through to the end.

clue.text: Sounds like unprepossessing fruit

indicators.note: says the word for unattractive ones is heard, then spelt differently

parts.note: unprepossessing ones are ugly ones, uglies

explanation.surface: A remark that some fruit is unattractive to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus hybrid of grapefruit and tangerine with a wrinkled, unattractive skin, sold under a trade name.

clue.text: Punish by separation?

parts.note: to criticise or beat someone severely, and also to dismantle something into its components

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to thrash an opponent and to dismantle into pieces.

clue.text: Not a form of rebate from the Inland Revenue, however

definitions.text: Not a form of rebate from the Inland Revenue, however

parts.words: Not a form of rebate from the Inland Revenue, however
parts.note: the words could suggest money coming back from the tax office, but the item is the paperwork sent to it

explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the former British tax authority.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual form declaring income to the tax authorities, despite sounding like a refund.

clue.text: He could get riled if made to work

definitions.text: He could get riled if made to work

indicators.note: making the letters work means putting them into a new order

explanation.surface: A lazy man gets annoyed when forced to do some work.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout who avoids labour would be irritated by having to toil.

clue.text: Programme for a girl with inside information

indicators.note: with something inside means the information word sits within the girl's name

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A schedule drawn up for a young woman who has insider knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be dealt with at a meeting is its programme.

clue.text: Make the scale in fighting fashion

definitions.text: Make the scale in fighting fashion

parts.words: Make the scale in fighting fashion
parts.note: climbing walls with ladders as part of a military assault

explanation.definitionFit: The historical term for storming fortifications by climbing them with ladders.

clue.text: Outstanding standard bearer

parts.note: sounds like an excellent person, but describes a pole standing out that carries a banner

explanation.definitionFit: A tall pole that holds up a banner or ensign stands out above its surroundings.

clue.text: Way Eric lost proves more expensive

indicators.note: way here means manner or fashion, so the letters are put into another form

explanation.surface: A man named Eric takes a wrong road and the detour costs him more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way' looks like a road but signals the rearrangement of ERIC and LOST together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dearer costs a greater price.

clue.text: Whale said to be worth a considerable amount

indicators.note: said means the phrase is spoken and the result spelt as heard

parts.note: something worth a great deal could be said to cash a lot

explanation.surface: A whale is reputed to be very valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the sperm whale.

clue.text: At a stretch to draw

parts.note: taken as written
a tract is a stretch of land

explanation.surface: Pulling something out to its full length.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to pull it in or entice it.

clue.text: High range of service provided

parts.note: Mass is a church service
provided that means on condition, if

explanation.surface: A broad selection of church services on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact group of mountains forming a single upland block.

clue.text: Germ-free for a short month I note

parts.note: Sept is the short form of September
taken as written
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A sterile period lasting a brief month.
explanation.definitionFit: Free from bacteria and other contaminants, as a sterile dressing is.

clue.text: French tipple ordered by inclination

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a nod is an inclination of the head

explanation.surface: Someone orders an aniseed drink in a bar with a nod of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured aperitif made in France, a brand of pastis.

clue.text: Lie about at an Israeli resort

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Lounging about on holiday at a seaside town in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: A port and holiday town on the Red Sea at Israel's southern tip.

clue.text: One put her out at once

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone evicted a woman without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for immediately after that, straight away.

clue.text: Plant found by Greek deity on the outskirts of Surrey

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A flower discovered by a god at the edge of a Home Counties county.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flower of the violet family with velvety petals.

clue.text: Fixed allowance covering a day in Spain for medical treatment

indicators.note: covering says the allowance word wraps round the Spanish word

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance
dia is Spanish for day

explanation.surface: A set allowance for a day in Spain covers someone's medical treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment of disease such as cancer by X-rays or other rays.

clue.text: Capital in which a large quantity of beer is held

parts.note: a tun is a large cask of beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city where a huge amount of beer is stored.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital city of Tunisia in North Africa.

clue.text: A pretty cold old winger in form

indicators.note: putting the letters in another form rearranges them

explanation.surface: A good-looking, chilly old wing player in top form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old winger' sounds like a veteran footballer, but is an extinct flying reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct flying reptile from the age of the dinosaurs.
